bullets.title: June CPI Shocker: Headline -0.4% MoM, Core Flat — Biggest Drop Since COVID
bullets.body: June CPI fell 0.4% MoM (vs. -0.1% expected) and 3.5% YoY (vs. 3.8% expected); core CPI printed 0.0% MoM and 2.6% YoY, both below consensus. Supercore services dropped 0.2% MoM, the largest decline since the pandemic, while shelter rose just 0.1% MoM—its smallest monthly gain since Jan 2021. 3-month annualized CPI collapsed from 8.2% to 2.8%.

bullets.title: Rate-Hike Odds Collapse to ~13-14% on CPI Miss; 2-Year Yield -10bps
bullets.body: Short-term rate futures surged and 2-year Treasury yields fell 10bps after the CPI print, as traders slashed Fed rate-hike bets. Rate-hike probability for September fell to ~13-14%. SPY futures rose 0.3% immediately following the release; QQQ and IWM each gained ~1.5%.

bullets.title: Warsh: 'Mission Accomplished' Not My View; Fed Has 'No Tolerance' for High Inflation
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh explicitly rejected the 'mission accomplished' inflation narrative after today's CPI data, calling the fight ongoing and troubling. He characterized inflation as a policy choice rather than an external force, pledged Fed independence, and signaled internal debate ('family fight') on the timing and extent of policy tools. UBS called his tone 'resolutely hawkish.'

bullets.title: NVDA H200 Shipments to China Begin; Volume Described as 'Trivial' by Officials
bullets.body: U.S. officials confirmed the first NVIDIA H200 GPU shipments to China and Hong Kong, with Commerce's Kessler calling the volume 'very few' and 'trivial.' The cleared licenses cover ~10 Chinese entities. Large-scale H200 shipments have not resumed; only small initial batches have cleared the licensing and customs pipeline after months of delays.

bullets.title: UBER in Advanced Talks to Acquire Delivery Hero for ~$13B at Significant Premium
bullets.body: Uber is in advanced takeover discussions with German food-delivery company Delivery Hero, valued at just under $13B; Uber is planning to bid well above the recent trading price. UBER shares slipped ~2.5% intraday on the news.

bullets.title: AAPL: KeyBanc Cuts to Underweight on Device Demand Weakness, AI Talks with PrismML
bullets.body: KeyBanc downgraded Apple to underweight from sector weight, citing weaker device demand and slower US service revenue growth; shares were down ~1.1% premarket. Separately, Apple is in talks with startup PrismML about shrinking AI models to run natively on iPhone, a potential on-device inference play.

bullets.title: META: Bearish Options Flow Dominates; AI Layoff Targeting Allegations Add Legal Risk
bullets.body: META carried the most bearish options flow of any tracked name during the session. The company also faces a Reuters-reported lawsuit alleging it used AI-powered software to identify workers with medical conditions for mass layoffs—raising potential discrimination liability.

bullets.title: NVDA + SMCI: AMD Helios/Vera Rubin AI Infrastructure Update; Supermicro CEO Color
bullets.body: Supermicro CEO discussed next-gen AI server infrastructure: AMD Helios has public customer traction with no pushback on double-wide racks; Vera Rubin mentioned as key upcoming product. Global supply chain is operational across US, Asia, and Europe. Storage (PCIe Gen 6, KV cache offload, software-defined) emerging as primary design consideration. NVDA also partnering with Mitsubishi Heavy on data center cooling and power.

bullets.title: HUBS: Negative Channel Check — Tracking 10-15% Below Plan
bullets.body: A RayJay analyst flagged HubSpot tracking 10-15% below plan for the current period. Enterprise SaaS peers including WDAY, TEAM, and NOW also sold off following IBM's negative preannouncement, which spooked the sector.

bullets.title: MU: Whale Loaded $16.3M in Short-Dated Calls Pre-Close; +40% Overnight, $6.5M Gain
bullets.body: A large whale accumulated $16.3M in short-dated Micron calls less than an hour before the prior session's close; MU gapped up overnight and the position gained 40%, netting ~$6.5M. A separate source flagged continued whale accumulation on an intraday basis.

bullets.title: TSEM: Japan-Backed 300mm SiPho/SiGe Expansion Announced; CPO Delay Flagged
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor announced a Japanese government-backed expansion of 300mm Silicon Photonics, Silicon Germanium, and advanced packaging capacity targeting $1.2B net profit. However, a separate tweet flagged a CPO (customer product order) delay as a near-term headwind. MRVL and TSEM are also being called out as a 'winner couple in AI Photonics.'

bullets.title: ORCL: Down 30.5% Over Past Month, Trading at 1-Year Lows
bullets.body: Oracle has plunged 30.5% over the past month and is now trading at a 1-year low. No new negative catalyst flagged in the window; stock appears to be reflecting macro/sector re-rating pressure.

bullets.title: AVGO: Broadcom Revenue Could Double via MediaTek Integration by Decade's End
bullets.body: A fintwit analyst with semiconductor industry contacts argues that Broadcom's revenue could grow significantly through the MTK acquisition, potentially doubling MediaTek's current business size by end of the decade. Industry concerns about margin pressure are characterized as overblown.

bullets.title: AMZN: Anthropic Stake 'Not Reflected' in Current Valuation; $3T Hypothetical = 20% of AMZN MCap
bullets.body: A fintwit analyst argues Anthropic's value is not priced into AMZN. If Anthropic IPO'd at $3T, AMZN's stake would represent ~20% of its current market cap—and a 'normal' multiple on AWS alone could already justify AMZN's full valuation, implying Anthropic is essentially free in the stock.

bullets.title: NY State Data Center Moratorium: Analysts Discount Impact, Cite Executive Order Reversibility
bullets.body: New York became the first state to impose a one-year data center moratorium via executive order (not law). A JMP Citizens analyst and other fintwit voices argue it can be reversed and that the US market is large enough to absorb 25+ state-level moratoriums without material capacity impact.

bullets.title: SPY Options: $1.6B Call Wall at 757, $375M Dark Pool Print; Positive Gamma Absorbing Volatility
bullets.body: SPY's largest call wall sits at 757 with $1.6B notional; a $375M dark pool print was also flagged. Positive gamma exposure continues to increase, providing shock absorption against volatility. The call wall has since moved up to 760 with $1.4B notional.

bullets.title: Macro AI Phase Shift: From Infrastructure Trade to Model-Lab Trade in 2026
bullets.body: An analyst argues the 2023-2025 AI trade was infrastructure-focused (TSMC, NVDA, memory, power). In 2026, value capture is shifting to model labs—Anthropic ARR has grown from $9B at end-2024 to $44B+ YTD. AI labs can now cut sticker prices while protecting unit economics, pressuring downstream infrastructure margins.

bullets.title: NBIS: $1B+ Compute Deal with Reflection AI Announced; Stock Falls 5% on News
bullets.body: Nebius signed a $1B+ compute agreement with Reflection AI for GB300 GPU access through 2029. Reflection AI also signed a multi-billion dollar deal with SpaceX. Despite the announcement, NBIS fell 5% on the news, raising questions about deal quality or market skepticism on contract economics.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Commits to 100% of Output from 1.6GW Arkansas Solar Project Starting 2029
bullets.body: Google agreed to purchase the entire energy output from Steel River Energy Center in Arkansas—a 1.6GW solar facility expected to begin operations in 2029, described as the biggest solar project of its kind to break ground in the US.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Escalation: Iran Attacks Kuwait/Bahrain; Oil Futures Volatile; Hormuz Clarified
bullets.body: Iran fired missiles and drones at Kuwait and Bahrain, with multiple explosions reported on Qeshm Island. Oil futures spiked then pared gains after Trump clarified the Strait of Hormuz remains open to all shipping except Iran and replaced the proposed 20% cargo fee with trade deals. WTI briefly turned negative before recovering near $78-79/bbl.
